A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DiffSensei and MangaZero research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–G are readable and can be matched across additions, renumbering and repagination.

before.justification: v1 reports original MangaZero and Manga109 evaluations, human preferences, quantitative ablations and generated examples.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds a human evaluation of the MLLM component and a qualitative ground-truth comparison.

M1.justification: The feature extractors, masked character attention, dialog embedding, MLLM adapter, two-stage training objectives and inference weighting remain unchanged. The new experiments evaluate existing components.

E1.justification: Both versions train on MangaZero and evaluate on MangaZero and Manga109. Real-person and long-story demonstrations already appear in v1; the added appendix comparisons introduce no distinct dataset, domain or task coverage.

E2.justification: The new human comparison in v2 Fig. 12 includes the no-MLLM variant, previously evaluated through automatic and qualitative ablations. The five external baselines in Table 2 and Fig. 5 remain unchanged; the newly cited RelationBooth is not evaluated.

E3.justification: v2 adds a human full-model-versus-no-MLLM comparison using five preference criteria, extending the earlier automatic and qualitative component evaluations. Existing splits, training settings and automated metrics are unchanged. The participant and page-set counts newly documented in Appendix C do not establish a revision to the existing study.

E4.justification: Appendix D adds human evidence testing the MLLM component's effect on perceived alignment, consistency and quality. Appendix B adds a qualitative comparison with ground-truth panels. The existing component, sampling-rate and weighting ablations and failure cases are retained.

E5.justification: The added human results use the existing point-estimate preference reporting practice. Neither version provides confidence intervals, error bars, significance tests or repeated-run counts; the qualitative illustration mentioning different random seeds is retained.

E6.justification: v2 Fig. 12 newly reports full-model versus no-MLLM preferences, including 83.4% versus 16.6% for text alignment and 81.3% versus 18.7% overall. Fig. 9 adds a ground-truth comparison. Tables 2–4 and the original human preference results in Fig. 5 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The problem formulation and Equations 1–6 retain the same definitions, attention mask and loss formulation. Neither version adds theoretical propositions, proofs or revised mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The main contributions remain the customized manga-generation task, MangaZero dataset and DiffSensei framework. Claims about dynamic character adaptation, layout control, generalization and superiority over existing methods retain their original scope.

C2.justification: v2 newly interprets its ground-truth comparison as showing character alignment close to or better than the original panels. It also discusses the human ablation as supporting the MLLM's visual appeal and text compatibility. Existing applicability limits, failure explanations and identity-versus-text tradeoffs remain.

D1.justification: Appendix C newly specifies 15 evaluators, 10 anonymized page sets per evaluator, rating aggregation and the evaluation interface. The abstract changes promised code, model and dataset release to stated availability, although the introduction retains future-tense dataset-release wording.

R1.justification: v2 adds RelationBooth as reference 32 in the discussion of customized generation. The broader positioning and novelty arguments remain unchanged; most other citation differences are renumbering.

P1.justification: v2 removes a redundant related-work summary, makes small wording edits and adds short appendix passages. It also changes author order, identifies corresponding authors and adds an acknowledgement. The overall section and appendix organization is retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds three appendix figures: the ground-truth comparison, human-evaluation interface and MLLM preference chart. Existing figures are retained, with subsequent renumbering and relocation; the table structures and overall two-column layout remain substantially unchanged.

improvement.justification: The new human ablation supplies direct perceptual evidence for the central MLLM component, while Appendix C makes human evaluation more transparent. These are useful, limited gains over v1's existing ablations. The ground-truth comparison remains illustrative, and the new preference results lack uncertainty estimates, so the revision does not substantially strengthen the paper overall.
